CZ Register Extract (§ 435, status, activities)

Keeps a Czech subject's entry in the public register as data, composes the statement § 435 občanského zákoníku requires on your documents from it, and warns about partners the register no longer shows as active.

Version19.0.1.0.0
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresaccount, l10n_cz

What it is for

A Czech business has to state on its documents which register it is entered in and under which oddíl and vložka. Odoo's Czech localization gives the company a single free-text field, Trade Registry, for that statement. It is typed once and then forgotten — and goes on being printed after the seat, and with it the court, has changed.

This module:

  • keeps the three coordinates — Rejstřík (the register), Rejstříkový soud (the court keeping it) and Spisová značka (oddíl and vložka) — as separate fields, on your company and on any contact;
  • composes the statement from them, in correct Czech, and keeps the company's Trade Registry in step, so that it is printed on invoices;
  • shows on each Czech contact what the register says about it: status, dates of establishment and dissolution, předmět podnikání and činnosti (scope of business), and previous names and seats;
  • warns on an invoice or bill when the register shows the partner as dissolved, historical or suspended.

The data is typed by hand or filled from ARES by partner_autocomplete_ares_cz.

Legal background

§ 435 odst. 1 občanského zákoníku requires every entrepreneur to state the name and seat on business documents (obchodní listiny) and in information made available to the public by remote access — a website. Beyond that:

  • an entrepreneur entered in the obchodní rejstřík states that entry including the oddíl and vložka;
  • one entered in another public register (veřejný rejstřík) states the entry in that register;
  • one entered in no public register states the entry in another evidence — for a sole trader, the živnostenský rejstřík;
  • an identifying number (IČO), if one was assigned, is stated too.

The public registers are six — obchodní rejstřík, spolkový rejstřík, nadační rejstřík, rejstřík ústavů, rejstřík společenství vlastníků jednotek and rejstřík obecně prospěšných společností (§ 1 of zákon č. 304/2013 Sb.) — and each is kept by a rejstříkový soud: the Městský soud v Praze or a krajský soud.

Setting it up

Settings → Companies, open your Czech company. Above Trade Registry are three new fields:

Field Example
Rejstřík Obchodní rejstřík
Rejstříkový soud Městský soud v Praze
Spisová značka C 12345 — oddíl and vložka as the register writes them

From them the module composes the statement and writes it into Trade Registry, which Odoo's Czech localization prints on invoices:

Obchodní rejstřík vedený Městským soudem v Praze, oddíl C, vložka 12345

  • The statement names the register and the court keeping it rather than saying zapsaná or zapsaný, so it is correct whatever the legal form.
  • The court is put in the instrumental (Městský soud → Městským soudem, Krajský soud → Krajským soudem). The vedený … soudem and oddíl / vložka wording is used only for the six public registers.
  • Any other register is written as entered, with the authority after a comma and the number as číslo zápisu: …. A sole trader who enters only Živnostenský rejstřík gets just that.
  • A number that is not an oddíl and a vložka is printed whole, as spisová značka ….

Your own wording wins. If you type something else into Trade Registry, the module leaves it alone from then on. The composed statement is also shown, editable, as § 435 statement on the contact behind the company; an edit there reaches Trade Registry too and sticks until a coordinate changes again. Clearing all three coordinates clears the statement the module wrote.

The register on a contact

Tab Register (CZ) on a contact in Czechia (or with no country):

Group Fields
Zápis Rejstřík, Rejstříkový soud, Spisová značka, Datum vzniku, § 435 statement
Stav Stav v rejstříku, Datum zániku, Register checked (when the register was last read)

Below them, filled from the register and read-only:

  • Předmět podnikání a činnosti — what the entry says the subject does (předmět podnikání, předmět činnosti, doplňková činnost, účel), each with the day it was entered and the day it was deleted. These are the entry's own words, not the statistical CZ-NACE code.
  • Předchozí názvy a sídla — previous names and registered seats with their validity, useful for matching an old document to today's partner.

With partner_autocomplete_ares_cz installed, picking a company from the ARES suggestions or running Actions → Update on the contact fills all of it; nothing needs setting up. A sole trader who is in no public register but is in the živnostenský rejstřík gets Živnostenský rejstřík as the register.

Partners that are no longer active

When Stav v rejstříku is Zaniklý, Historický or Pozastavený:

  • a yellow banner at the top of the contact says the subject is not active, with the date of dissolution if known; the status can be shown as a column in the contact list;
  • an invoice, credit note or receipt of a company whose fiscal country is Czechia shows a warning naming the status, the date and when it was checked in the register. On a vendor bill it adds that the supplier may not have existed at the time of supply, so the right to deduct VAT should be checked;
  • when such a document is posted, the warning is also written to its chatter.

The warning never blocks posting. A final invoice or a late bill from a wound-up partner can be perfectly legitimate; the date on the document decides, and only a person can judge that.

To see every such partner at once, open Accounting → Customers → Neaktivní subjekty (CZ), or use the filter Neaktivní subjekty (CZ) in any contact list — customers, vendors or contacts.

Limitations

  • Odoo's Czech localization prints Trade Registry on invoices only, under the label Trade registry: (in Czech Zápis v obchodním rejstříku:), also when the statement names another register. § 435 also covers orders, letters and the website; put the statement there yourself.
  • The statement is deliberately not the usual zapsaná v obchodním rejstříku vedeném …. If you prefer that wording, type it into Trade Registry.
  • Only Městský soud and Krajský soud are declined. Anything else is printed as entered, which may read stiffly. Check the statement once.
  • There is no list of filed financial statements: they are in the sbírka listin, which ARES does not provide.
  • The status is as current as the last lookup; nothing refreshes it on a schedule. Without the ARES module the status, dates and lists stay empty unless you enter them by hand.
